display.purpose: Hero headline only. Uppercase. Hollow-stroke and acid-fill variants.

headline.purpose: Section h2 titles. Uppercase, tight leading.

title.purpose: Card names, panel headings, rate titles.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, nav links, button text, form labels, tags. Most-used role.

serif-accent.purpose: One italic line per section below the headline. Tonal counterpoint only.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Pillar card hover. Combines depth lift with diffuse acid glow.

shadows.name: button-glow
shadows.purpose: Acid-fill button hover only. Soft halo, 20% opacity. Never at rest.

motion.name: ease-out-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions and enter animations.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: Hero and section entrance. Staggered 0.2s per element.

motion.name: glitch-cycle
motion.purpose: Periodic glitch on display text. One element per viewport maximum.

motion.name: scan-line
motion.purpose: Scanline bar sweep on section overlays.

breakpoints.name: mobile

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.notes: Reduced padding, compressed gaps, two-column layouts preserved.

narrative.overview:
SPCTR's design system is an operational surface — a dark intelligence brief that surfaces only what needs to be seen. The visual language is borrowed from classified infrastructure: narrow-channel text, hard geometric type, earned color signals. Nothing decorates. Everything informs.

The palette is unusually wide for a brand site — seven named accent colors — but the system holds through strict rationing. Accent colors appear as eyebrow markers, card distinguishers, and glitch channels, never as fills or backgrounds. Signal Green is the lone exception: it marks confirmation, activation, and primary action at no more than 15% of any surface. The ground stays void-black. The signal earns its moment.

Typography pairs heavy geometric uppercase display (KH Interference) against Space Mono for all UI text, with Playfair Display italic appearing once per section as a deliberate tonal break — the single moment of curve in an otherwise hard-edged system.
keyCharacteristics: Deep void-black ground with tonal surface layering (void → near-void → panel surface)
One primary accent (Signal Green) plus six supporting chromatic channels, all strictly rationed
Parallelogram clip-path buttons: the signature shape, non-negotiable
Monospaced UI throughout — no humanist sans anywhere in the interface
Glitch, scanlines, and crosshair cursor as earned operational texture
KH Interference + Playfair italic as the type system's defining tension

rules.name: The Rationed Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Green and all six accent colors are state markers and section identifiers, not fill colors. Any screen where accent colors collectively exceed 15% of visible surface area has broken the system.

rules.name: The Seven-Channel Rule
rules.body: Each section is assigned one eyebrow color. That color appears nowhere else in that section. The variety in the palette exists to give each section its own operational frequency, not to create a rainbow.

rules.name: The Mono-First Rule
rules.body: Every UI string — buttons, labels, nav, form fields, metadata — runs in Space Mono. No humanist or geometric sans enters the interface. Fall back to system monospace, never to a sans-serif.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display appears at most once per visible section: one italic line below the headline. Never inside cards, never on buttons, never repeated.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never carry ambient shadows at rest. Shadow is a hover state, not a resting aesthetic. Use tonal surface shifts and 1px Boundary Line borders for resting depth.

dos: Do use the parallelogram clip-path on all primary buttons.
Do assign exactly one eyebrow accent color per section.
Do keep all UI text in Space Mono.
Do limit Playfair Display to one italic line per section.
Do introduce surface depth with tonal background shifts before reaching for shadows.
Do support prefers-reduced-motion — all animations are cosmetic.
Do keep Void Black as the absolute background ground.
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient).
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively — the nav blur is the only permitted exception.
Don't let Signal Green fill more than 15% of any screen.
Don't use bubbly SaaS optimism: rounded cards, pastel gradients, friendly illustrations.
Don't build hero-metric templates (large number, gradient accent, supporting stats).
Don't add border-radius to any interactive component.
Don't stack multiple glitch text elements in the same viewport.
Don't increase the scanline overlay opacity above 8%.
Don't use bright or saturated backgrounds — accent colors are signals, never grounds.
